root_causes.description: The checkout pod's container was killed and restarted during the incident window, dropping the checkout service's inbound server request rate to zero while the container churned.

evidence.query_or_id: Killing: Container checkout definition changed, will be restarted (count=1)
evidence.observed_value: container 'checkout' killed for restart (count=1); Started/Created events count=2
evidence.expected_baseline: no container kill/restart events for checkout during steady state

evidence.observed_value: p50=0.000, mean=0.018, max=0.057 req/s (traffic collapses to zero)
evidence.expected_baseline: steady inbound server request rate well above 0

root_causes.description: Checkout pod working-set memory spiked roughly 50x above baseline at the start of the window, a plausible trigger for an OOM-kill and container restart.

Kubernetes events also show the pod sandbox (pause container) repeatedly failing image pulls (ErrImagePull/ImagePullBackOff), which can independently drive pod churn and restart loops on the checkout pod.

evidence.observed_value: pause container image pull failures / BackOff (count=4)
evidence.expected_baseline: no image pull failures in steady state
pause sandbox image available, no back-off

remediation_steps: Roll-restart the checkout deployment to clear the crashed/restarting container: kubectl -n otel-demo rollout restart deployment/checkout
Inspect checkout container memory limits/requests alongside the observed working-set spike; raise limits or fix the leak so the container stops being killed and restarted
Resolve the pause-container image pull failures (ErrImagePull/ImagePullBackOff) so the pod sandbox can be created reliably and restart loops cease
Verify recovery by confirming checkout server request_rate returns to baseline and no further Killing/Started events appear in get_pod_events
